A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ACE-Merging with the same authors, research objective, and benchmark suite. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original vision and language merging results, component ablations, sensitivity experiments, and empirical weight-distribution and heterogeneity analyses, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and additionally reports isotropic-baseline comparisons and measured merging runtime and peak GPU memory.

M1.justification: The stated central computation changes: v1 Eq. (10) uses expert weights Wt in the fusion numerator, whereas v2 Eq. (14) uses centered task updates. The structural residual likewise changes from expert weights to uncentered task updates in v2 Eq. (17), and Algorithm 1 is revised accordingly. These materially alter the written procedure; the PDFs do not establish corresponding code changes or experimental reruns.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 8-, 14-, and 20-task vision sets, GLUE evaluations, and Appendix C.1 multilingual QA, coding, and mathematical-reasoning benchmarks. The new efficiency measurements reuse existing task settings.

E2.justification: v2 adds Iso-C and Iso-CTS to both the nine-setting vision comparison and the GPT-2 comparison in Tables 1–2. Appendix B also adds measured overhead comparisons against WUDI, TSV-M, and Iso-CTS. This substantially strengthens the evaluated comparator set; the existing accuracy baselines remain.

E3.justification: Appendix B introduces runtime and peak-memory evaluation on one NVIDIA A800 with 80 GB memory, using ViT-L/14 with eight tasks and GPT-2 with seven tasks, and specifying 1000 WUDI iterations. Retained benchmark configurations and stated ACE hyperparameters are unchanged.

E4.justification: The component ablations and plotted diagnostic analyses are retained. v2 removes the kfrac = 0.6 sensitivity point when combining v1 Tables 5–6 into Table 5, and adds empirical runtime/memory analysis alongside the existing asymptotic comparison.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies benchmark run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v2 introduces no uncertainty estimates for its new comparisons or profiling. The weight-distribution statistics in Figure 3 are unchanged.

E6.justification: The added Iso-C/Iso-CTS results materially change rankings: Iso-CTS exceeds ACE in five of nine vision settings, including 90.1 versus 89.5 on ViT-L/14 with 20 tasks. New Table 6 reports ACE at 4.32 seconds/2.04 GB and 4.70 seconds/1.02 GB in the two profiling settings. Existing ACE benchmark scores remain unchanged apart from rounding; the kfrac = 0.6 results, 91.17 and 73.71, are omitted.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 changes from proportionality between input covariance and update covariance to alignment of the expected per-sample gradient Gram matrix with the input second moment. Appendix A.3 replaces the covariance derivation with an expected update-Gram derivation and approximate assumptions. v2 also corrects the centering dimensions and removes the assertion that centered and uncentered quadratic forms share eigenvectors.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion narrow consistent state-of-the-art superiority to strong overall performance among data-free baselines. The introduction drops the claim of surpassing data-dependent and test-time vision methods, while Section 5.2 acknowledges Iso-CTS wins. The theoretical contribution is also framed more cautiously as informative second-order structure rather than the earlier covariance relationship.

C2.justification: Figure 3 and Appendix A.3 now interpret the histograms as supporting the approximate zero-mean assumption, removing their claimed support for residual-input decoupling. Appendix B adds the runtime-versus-memory tradeoff with TSV-M, and B.1 explicitly characterizes extreme hyperparameter limits as sanity checks rather than practical operating regimes.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability URL, hardware and iteration information for profiling, and explicit implementation explanations for CSP broadcasting and normalization using original task-vector energy. Existing model-specific regularization strengths and default threshold/rank settings are retained.

R1.justification: v2 removes the forgetting-aware-pruning citation by Huang, Cheng, and Wang, which was reference 25 in v1, and qualifies WUDI's relationship to the proposed statistical interpretation. The related-work taxonomy and most cited works remain; publication-metadata updates do not constitute new references.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, methodology, experimental discussion, conclusion, and substantial appendix passages are extensively rewritten. Terminology shifts toward second-moment proxies, implementation explanations expand, and the ablation discussion is consolidated. This is broad editorial revision beyond the added scientific content.

P2.justification: Tables 1–2 gain comparator rows, the two sensitivity tables become one, and a new overhead table is added. Algorithm 1 is reformatted, captions are revised, and appendix figures and tables move. The plotted contents themselves and the overall visual design remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The stronger baseline comparisons, qualified superiority claims, and measured efficiency evidence make v2 more credible and informative. The theoretical revision also removes the unjustified eigenvector-preservation assertion. These gains are tempered by an unresolved inconsistency between centered-update fusion in Eq. (14) and expert-weight limits in Appendix B.1, plus the omitted sensitivity point. Overall, transparency improves, but the central formulation is not fully reconciled.
